author: Mexico Daily Post
title: Parents of Murdered Australian Brothers Attend Final Hearing in Ensenada Murder Case
text:
ENSENADA, MEXICO — The trial surrounding the brutal 2024 murders of two Australian brothers and an American friend, a case that sparked international outrage over tourist safety in Mexico, entered its final phase on Thursday.
After a month of intensive hearings, the Baja California State Prosecutor’s Office and the defense for three of the primary suspects are scheduled to present closing arguments today. A verdict from the presiding judge is expected to be announced on Friday.
The proceedings have drawn significant international media attention and a somber atmosphere. In a poignant display of devotion, Martin and Debra Robinson—the parents of the Australian brothers, Callum and Jake—traveled from Australia to Ensenada to witness the final stages of the trial. “I know they would have wanted us to be here; they would do the same for us,” their father said during the proceedings.
The three victims—the Robinson brothers and their American friend, Jack Carter Rhoad—traveled to Baja California in April 2024 for a surfing trip. Shortly after arriving in the village of Punta San José, approximately 80 kilometers from the coastal city of Ensenada, the group was reported missing. Their bodies were discovered on May 3, 2024, inside a well near the village.
The prosecution has identified four primary suspects in the crime. Jesús Gerardo García, known by the local alias “el Kekas,” is accused of being the principal perpetrator. His accomplice, Ary Gisell Silva Raya, was sentenced to 20 years in prison last November after entering a plea deal for armed robbery. However, García and two other alleged collaborators, Irineo Francisco “N” and Ángel Jesús “N,” proceeded to a full trial.
During the proceedings, chilling details regarding the night of the murders were revealed. Silva Raya testified that García confessed to approaching the victims’ campsite armed with a 9mm pistol. According to her testimony, the victims attempted to defend themselves by throwing their belongings at the gunman. She further alleged that one of the victims pleaded for his life, but the requests were ignored.
State Prosecutor María Elena Andrade Ramírez told the press that “el Kekas” reportedly attempted to steal tires and other parts from the truck the trio was traveling in. When the victims resisted the robbery, the suspects allegedly executed them before hiding the bodies in a well.
The case remains a pivotal moment for Mexican authorities as they navigate the delicate balance of maintaining its status as a premier tourism destination while addressing the violent crimes that have tarnished its reputation.
